common_name: Superba Rodgersia (Bronze-Tinted Foliage Deep Pink Plumed Rodgersia)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Superba is a long-established rodgersia cultivar valued for its bronze-tinted young foliage and deep pink summer plumes.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade, along a pond edge or in a damp woodland bed. Superba produces large, deeply veined, palmate leaves that emerge with a bronze-purple tint before maturing toward green, topped in summer by tall, feathery plumes of deep pink flowers held well above the foliage, a taller and more floriferous older cultivar than many newer rodgersia selections bred mainly for foliage color. It needs reliably moist, even boggy soil to perform well and will scorch or wilt in dry conditions, so a spot near a water feature or low, damp corner of the garden suits it best. In hot Southern climates give it more shade than the mostly-sun exposure it tolerates further north, since intense summer sun combined with humidity stress can damage the foliage.
